title: The name won't resolve
briefing: The deploy scripts talk to a host they call 'api.internal' — but it doesn't
resolve, so every call fails with 'Could not resolve host'.
DNS doesn't know that name. The fix an operator reaches for: pin it in
/etc/hosts, which the resolver checks before DNS. Point api.internal at the
same box the status service runs on.
tips: `dig api.internal` returns nothing (NXDOMAIN). `dig +short status.internal` gives you the IP to reuse.
/etc/hosts lines are 'IP  name'. It's root-owned — become root with sudo -i to edit it.
objective: Make api.internal resolve to the status host (10.10.0.30) by adding it to /etc/hosts.
expert_objective: api.internal doesn't resolve. Map it to 10.10.0.30 in /etc/hosts.
hints: Find the target IP: `dig +short status.internal` → 10.10.0.30. Confirm the problem: `dig api.internal` is NXDOMAIN.
Edit /etc/hosts as root: `sudo -i`, then append the mapping.
As root: `echo "10.10.0.30 api.internal" >> /etc/hosts`, then check with `dig +short api.internal`.
solution:
dig +short status.internal
dig api.internal
sudo -i
echo "10.10.0.30 api.internal" >> /etc/hosts
dig +short api.internal
explanation: Name resolution checks /etc/hosts before it ever asks DNS. That makes /etc/hosts the quickest fix (and a common gotcha) when a name won't resolve — one 'IP  name' line and the host is reachable by that name. dig is how you see what a name currently resolves to, or that it doesn't.
